templates.name: enshrouded
templates.description: Enshrouded dedicated server — a survival, crafting and Action-RPG game set in a sprawling voxel continent. Enshrouded ships a WINDOWS-ONLY dedicated server (Steam app 2278520, oslist=windows), so this template runs it through GE-Proton. That detail is what makes the stock egg break: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/steamcmd:proton (built 2026-06-22, Debian 12 / glibc 2.36) ships GE-Proton10-34, whose lsteamclient shim implements SteamUtils008/009/010 but NOT SteamUtils011. Enshrouded 1.0 (2026-10-15) requires SteamUtils011, so the server dies during Steamworks init — before it ever writes enshrouded_server.log. The visible symptom is a bare exit-code-1 crash loop with `tail: cannot open './logs/enshrouded_server.log'`. This template pins ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/steamcmd:ubuntu_24.04 (Ubuntu 24.04 / glibc 2.39, ships libvulkan1 and Xvfb) and installs GE-Proton11-9 at install time (its lsteamclient exports SteamUtils011, 258 references). Xvfb is started before Proton because a headless Wine/Proton prefix needs an X display. GE-Proton11-9 is a glibc-2.38+ build, so it CANNOT run on the bookworm-based steamcmd:proton image — the distro, not just the Proton version, is part of the fix. Verified end-to-end on Catalyst: server reaches `[Session] 'HostOnline' (up)!` and listens on UDP 15637.

templates.name: fastdl
templates.description: Standalone FastDL (fast download) web server for Half-Life 1 and Source engine games. Serves client download content (maps, models, sounds, materials) from ./fastdl/<gamedir>/ with byte-Range support, 304 revalidation, correct MIME types and a browsable directory index — the HTTP features engines need to download custom content at line speed. Works with Counter-Strike 1.6, Garry's Mod, CS:S, TF2, HL2:DM, Sven Co-op and any game supporting sv_downloadurl. Upload content via SFTP into ./fastdl/<gamedir>/ (e.g. fastdl/cstrike/ or fastdl/garrysmod/), then set on each game server: sv_downloadurl "http://<node-ip>:<this-port>". The runtime is a single static Caddy binary on a minimal Alpine image — no database, no scripting, ~64 MB RAM. HL1/Source FastDL is plain HTTP; put a reverse proxy or CDN in front for HTTPS (it must pass Range requests through).
